2027-03-08.title: Monday of the Fourth Week of Lent
readings: I am about to create new heavens and a new earth
I will praise you, Lord, for you have rescued me
2027-03-08.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St John of God, religious (his collect may be used). On any weekday of this week the optional Mass of the Fourth Week of Lent may be used instead, with the Gospel of the man born blind (Micah 7:7–9; Psalm 27; John 9:1–41), especially where it was not read on Sunday.
2027-03-08.verse: Jesus said to him, “Go; your son will live.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and started on his way.
theo: Laetare Sunday has just lifted our eyes toward Easter, and today Isaiah carries that joy further. God speaks like an artist about to begin his greatest work: “For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.” Jerusalem will be a joy and its people a delight; “no more shall the sound of weeping be heard in it, or the cry of distress.” No infant will die after a few days, and the old will live out their years; people will build houses and live in them, plant vineyards and eat their fruit. It is the picture of a world healed of death and of wasted labour. The Psalm answers with the song of someone who has been brought back from the edge of the grave: “O LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you have healed me.” And it gives Lent one of its loveliest lines: “Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.”

The Gospel shows the new creation beginning in one household. Jesus has come back to Cana, where he changed water into wine. A royal official, probably a servant of Herod Antipas, walks some twenty-five kilometres up from Capernaum, because his son is dying. Jesus seems to answer coldly: “Unless you see signs and wonders you will not believe.” The father does not argue; he simply pleads: “Sir, come down before my little boy dies.” Then Jesus gives him not a sign but a word: “Go; your son will live.” And the man does the hardest thing a worried father can do: he turns round and walks home with nothing in his hands but that word. “The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and started on his way.” On the road his servants meet him: the boy is alive, and the fever left him at one in the afternoon, the very hour Jesus spoke. Faith that began as a cry becomes trust in a word, and ends as the faith of a whole household. Today we also remember St John of God (1495–1550), a Portuguese soldier and bookseller who, converted by a sermon of St John of Avila, spent the rest of his life gathering the sick and the poor of Granada into a hospital and caring for them with his own hands. From his companions grew the Brothers Hospitallers. He believed that every sick person was Christ, and he served them like a father carrying home a child.
outline: Ask: have you ever had to walk away from a problem with only a promise in your hands?
Isaiah's new heavens and new earth.
Point 2 · Go; your son will live
A father who believes the word.
St John of God and the healing of Christ.
“Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.”
live: Take one promise of God from today's readings and carry it with you all day, like the father walking home.
Like St John of God, visit or call someone who is ill, and pray with them if they wish.
2027-03-08.prayer: Lord God, you make all things new and turn our mourning into dancing. Give us the faith of the royal official, to believe your Son's word and set out on our way. Through the prayers of St John of God, give the sick tender care and make our hands ready to serve them. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The word that healed the official's son from far away is the same word that is spoken over the bread and wine at Mass. We believe it, and Christ is truly present, giving life.

quick: God promises new heavens and a new earth, a world without weeping.
A father believes Jesus' word and his son lives.
St John of God served the sick poor as Christ himself.
2027-03-08.action: Visit, phone or pray with one sick person today.
2027-03-08.question: Do I believe Jesus' word even when I see no sign yet?

family.explain: A father's little boy was very ill. He asked Jesus to come. Jesus said: go home, your son will live. The father believed and walked home, and on the way he heard that his son was well. We can trust what Jesus says.
family.intention: We pray for sick children and their parents.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we know who is sick, and how can we help them this week?”

illus: A nurse in a district hospital near Thrissur kept a small card in her pocket through thirty years of night duty. On it she had written: Every bed has Christ in it. When she retired, the younger nurses found the card worn soft at the edges. One of them said: we thought she was just kind; now we know whom she was looking at.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word gives life even from afar. Speak your word over us and over those we love. Amen.
share: I am about to create new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17). Where do I long for God to make something new?
The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him (John 4:50). When have I had to trust without seeing?
I was sick and you took care of me (Matthew 25:36). Whom is Christ asking me to care for?
pm.resp: I will praise you, Lord, for you have rescued me.
interc: For sick children and their families, that they may know God's healing and peace.
For doctors, nurses and all who work in hospitals, through the prayers of St John of God.
For those whose faith is waiting for a sign, that they may trust Christ's word.
For the dying, that joy may come to them with the morning of the resurrection.
For our group, that we may carry Christ's word into the week.
pm.close: Father, you turn mourning into dancing. Make us believers in your Son's word and servants of the sick. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today God speaks through Isaiah like a builder about to begin: for I am about to create new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17). No more weeping, no more children dying, no more wasted work. That is where God is taking the world, and that is where Lent is taking us: to Easter, the first morning of the new creation.

In the Gospel a father comes to Jesus because his little boy is dying. Jesus says: unless you see signs and wonders you will not believe. The father does not argue; he only begs: sir, come down before my little boy dies.

And Jesus says only: go; your son will live (John 4:50). Think of that walk home. No sign, no proof, only a word. The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and started on his way. On the road the good news meets him: the fever left the boy at the very hour Jesus spoke. That is what faith is: walking on the strength of Christ's word.

Today we remember St John of God, who once lived a wild and wandering life. After his conversion he filled a house in Granada with the sick and the poor and served them with his own hands, because he saw Christ in every one of them. Let us believe the word of Jesus, and let that faith become hands that serve the sick. Amen.
kids: Children, a father's son was very sick. Jesus said: go home, your son will live! The father believed Jesus and went home, and his son was well. When Jesus says something, we can trust him. Let us pray today for a child who is sick.

intro: God makes all things new, a father believes the word of Jesus, and a saint turns faith into care for the sick.

q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.
And the one who was seated on the throne said, “See, I am making all things new.”
points.apply: Bring to God in prayer one situation that seems hopeless, and ask him to make it new.

sub: A word instead of a sign.
q: O LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you have healed me.
Jesus said to him, “Go; your son will live.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and started on his way.
points.apply: Each morning this week, read one verse of the Gospel and act on it before evening.

q: You have turned my mourning into dancing; you have taken off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy,
I was naked and you gave me clothing, I was sick and you took care of me, I was in prison and you visited me.
points.apply: Visit one sick or housebound person before Sunday, and bring them Christ's peace.

concl: God is making all things new, and Easter is the first morning.
We believe the word of Jesus and walk on it, and our faith becomes care for the sick.
2027-03-08.resolve: Visit or call one sick person this week, and pray with them.
